output.headline: EU €675k fixed-amount Lot 3 grant for media freedom & pluralism in Syria; restricted CFP, concept note due 18 May 2026.
fit_reasoning: CSIM's core mandate — independent journalism training, editorial coaching, journalist protection, and anti-disinformation work — maps directly onto Lot 3 priorities: strengthening independent media, protecting journalists/bloggers, and raising public awareness on media freedom.

Operational nodes in Gaziantep, Erbil, and Qamishli provide credible field reach into Northwest Syria, KRI, and Northeast Syria — the primary geographic areas of concern for the EU's Syria re-engagement strategy.
Multi-platform Arabic and Kurdish content production directly addresses the pluralism dimension of Lot 3 and the EU's emphasis on inclusive, multi-community outreach.

CSIM has delivered four sub-million-EUR grants on time with no audit qualifications (KPMG Türkiye, clean 2024), demonstrating the financial management track record EU evaluators weight heavily at eligibility stage.
Existing relationships with SIDA, Free Press Unlimited, and Internews (subaward) signal credibility within the media-development donor ecosystem that the EU Delegation will recognise.

Network of vetted Syrian journalists, photographers, and fact-checkers constitutes a ready implementation asset that reduces start-up risk — a scoring advantage under 'design of the action' and 'capacity of the applicant'.

gap_analysis.gap: PADOR registration is listed as 'in progress'; PROSPECT submission requires a valid PADOR EuropeAid ID before the concept note can be submitted online.
gap_analysis.fix: Prioritise PADOR completion immediately; allow 2–3 weeks for EC validation. Target completion by 15 April 2026 to avoid last-minute IT issues.

gap_analysis.gap: CSIM has been a co-applicant on a USAID award and lead on one small EU project (~sub-million EUR); Lot 3 is a fixed €675k grant, but EU evaluators will scrutinise whether the lead applicant has managed EU grants of comparable scope independently.
gap_analysis.fix: Document the 2023 EU lead-applicant grant in detail (budget managed, reporting cycle, EC contact); if grant was <€300k, position the INGO co-applicant as the entity that elevates institutional credibility.

gap_analysis.gap: Co-applicant is described as 'in soft conversation' only; no confirmed INGO partner with PADOR registration and EU grant history is locked in.
gap_analysis.fix: Formalise a Letter of Intent with the INGO co-applicant before the information session (21 April 2026); ensure the partner has an active PADOR ID and can evidence EU grant management experience.

gap_analysis.gap: Co-financing: the call requires a minimum 10% co-financing (100% EU max only for applicants established in Syria per Corrigendum No.1; CSIM is registered in Türkiye, so 90% EU max applies, meaning at least 10% own/other funds needed).
gap_analysis.fix: CSIM's stated ~5% own reserves plus SIDA bridge financing may cover the gap, but this must be confirmed in writing. Secure a co-financing commitment letter from SIDA or another non-EU source before full application stage.

gap_analysis.gap: No explicit evidence of CSIM having a formal journalist digital-security or physical-protection programme — Lot 3 priority 2 specifically calls for 'effective protection of journalists, bloggers and other media workers'.
gap_analysis.fix: Either document existing protection activities (e.g. digital-security training delivered, relocation support provided) or bring a specialist sub-contractor (e.g. Committee to Protect Journalists, Reporters Without Borders affiliate) to fill this gap in the concept note.

red_flags: PADOR registration incomplete — submission is technically impossible without a validated EuropeAid ID; this is a hard blocker if not resolved well before 18 May 2026.

Lot 3 is the smallest lot (EUR 675k fixed, single award) — competition from larger, more established media-freedom INGOs (e.g. Internews, IMS, RSF) is likely intense; CSIM's smaller institutional profile is a scoring disadvantage on 'capacity'.
Co-financing gap: CSIM's ~5% own reserves may be insufficient to cover the ≥10% co-financing requirement without confirmed SIDA bridge financing in writing.

Corrigendum No.1 clarifies the 100% EU funding exemption applies only to the lead applicant established in Syria — CSIM is registered in Türkiye and does not qualify, increasing financial risk if co-financing cannot be confirmed.
conditions_for_bid: Complete PADOR registration and obtain a validated EuropeAid ID before 15 April 2026.
Confirm and formalise the INGO co-applicant with a signed Letter of Intent and verified PADOR registration before the 21 April 2026 information session.
Secure a written co-financing commitment (SIDA bridge or equivalent non-EU source) covering at least 10% of the EUR 675k budget (i.e., ≥EUR 67,500) before submitting the concept note.
next_steps: IMMEDIATE (this week): Escalate PADOR registration to highest internal priority; assign one staff member as sole owner; target EC validation by 10 April 2026.
BY 10 APRIL 2026: Contact SIDA programme officer to request a written co-financing commitment letter for up to EUR 75,000 bridge financing against the Lot 3 grant.

BY 15 APRIL 2026: Formalise the INGO co-applicant relationship with a signed Letter of Intent; confirm the partner's PADOR ID and EU grant eligibility; register for the 21 April online information session (email DELEGATION-SYRIA-FCA@eeas.europa.eu with max 2 participants).

BY 30 APRIL 2026: Complete the context/needs analysis for media freedom in Syria and draft the concept note narrative, ensuring Lot 3 priorities 1–3 are each explicitly addressed with CSIM-specific activities and measurable outputs.

BY 10 MAY 2026: Conduct an internal red-team review of the concept note against the evaluation grid (relevance 20pts + design 25pts); submit via PROSPECT no later than 16 May 2026 to allow for IT contingency before the 18 May 12:00 Brussels deadline.

output.tender_type_note: Restricted CFP (2-stage): concept note first, then invited full application; quality-scored, not lowest-price; narrative + design heavy.

notes: Lot 3 grant is a fixed amount: minimum and maximum are both EUR 675,000 — no budget flexibility; budget must be designed to exactly match this figure.
EU co-financing maximum is 90% for CSIM (Türkiye-registered); minimum 10% must come from non-EU sources.
Minimum EU co-financing floor is 70% of total eligible costs.
Indirect costs (overheads) are typically capped at 7% of direct eligible costs under EU standard grant contracts — verify in PRAG and full guidelines.

Payment schedule for EU grants typically follows: pre-financing advance on contract signature, interim payment(s) on report approval, balance on final report — exact schedule will be in the grant contract template.
No bid security or performance bond referenced in the guidelines; standard EU grant contract provisions apply.

eligibility_findings.requirement: Lead applicant must be a non-profit organisation or international organisation; must have legal personality.
eligibility_findings.rationale: CSIM is a registered Syrian-led nonprofit in Türkiye with legal personality evidenced by statutes; this satisfies the actor eligibility requirement.

eligibility_findings.requirement: Lead applicant must be registered in PADOR before submission via PROSPECT.
eligibility_findings.rationale: PADOR registration is in progress; must be completed and validated by EC before the concept note deadline of 18 May 2026.

eligibility_findings.requirement: Maximum EU co-financing is 90% of total eligible costs for applicants NOT established in the locations listed in Section 2.1.3 (i.e., not established in Syria); balance must come from non-EU sources.
eligibility_findings.rationale: CSIM is registered in Türkiye, not Syria, so the 100% exemption does not apply per Corrigendum No.1; the ~5% own reserves plus SIDA bridge must demonstrably cover the ≥10% co-financing requirement.

eligibility_findings.requirement: Co-applicant(s) must meet the same eligibility conditions as the lead applicant and must be registered in PADOR.
eligibility_findings.rationale: The intended INGO co-applicant is only in soft conversation; a confirmed, PADOR-registered EU-eligible partner must be formalised before concept note submission.

eligibility_findings.requirement: Actions must be implemented in Syria and/or directly benefit Syrian populations; geographic eligibility of the action.
eligibility_findings.rationale: CSIM operates field nodes in Gaziantep, Erbil, and Qamishli with a network of Syrian journalists across governorates, satisfying the geographic implementation requirement.

eligibility_findings.requirement: Applicants must not be in any of the exclusion situations listed in the PRAG (bankruptcy, fraud, conflict of interest, etc.); Declaration by the Lead Applicant required.
eligibility_findings.rationale: CSIM has a clean KPMG audit (2024) and no reported audit qualifications; Declaration of Honour is already drafted per intake notes.
